742510101.text: Many thanks for the invitation, Miss Guillotin. I presume this pure water was prepared specially for me?

742510102.text: Think nothing of it, Monsieur Neuvillette. It's an honor to have the Iudex of Fontaine take time out of his busy schedule to join me for a cup of... water.

742510103.text: Does the Fatui have some official business that you wish to discuss?

742510104.text: Not at all. This is a strictly personal visit. And there's no need to be so formal. I simply wanted to ask you about an old acquaintance.

742510105.text: An old acquaintance... Ah, you must be talking about Mr. Alain Guillotin? The great Lord-Artificer.

742510106.text: Exactly. What kind of person was he? I heard he was your subordinate in his youth.

742510108.text: Mr. Guillotin was an earnest and grounded young man. Even after being granted the title of White Cavalier of Protection, he never exhibited one iota of arrogance.

742510109.text: He spent most of his time studying machines. The world outside his own little bubble was of little interest to him.

742510110.text: Huh... So he was like that even when he was younger? I wonder if he was wise beyond his years or simply ignorant of the ways of the world.

742510111.text: However... He changed dramatically after losing his family and friends.

742510112.text: The Tower of Gestalt? And Elynas...

742510113.text: Indeed. When he and I signed the order to search the tower, he appeared... helpless.

742510114.text: It was the estrangement and alienation of the past that led to all that. He must have felt guilty, too.

742510115.text: Hmm... He became even more taciturn after that, and our interactions grew less frequent.

742510116.text: At the ceremony where he was given the title of Lord-Artificer, all he said was the following:

742510117.text: "A quiet, humble life is a surer path to happiness than the blind pursuit of endless perfection."

742510118.text: Heh... And that's exactly how he lived in his later years.

742510119.text: I guess he wasn't just saying that to the crowd. He was saying it to himself.

742510120.text: And what do you think about it all, Miss Guillotin?

742510121.text: Me? Hmph. I won't pass judgment on his epiphany or his way of life, just as he never told me how I should live my own.

742510122.text: But I have no intention of either following his path or of imitating his ideals. I'm my own person.

742510123.text: Heh... Thank you. You've helped me understand him better.

742510124.text: You're very welcome. It's a pleasure to share stories of the past with one of his family.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the vicinity of the Palais Mermonia to begin the tea party

742510201.text: And a pleasure to share stories of the past with you, Miss Guillotin, over this wonderful glass of water.

742510202.text: (Let's sit like this for a little while longer.)

742510204.text: Very well. Wherever you're going next, I wish you a smooth journey.
